message.content:
Translate the Heard Chrome extension's interface strings into Portuguese (pt, Brazilian, matching the website).

Source: /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/extension/i18n/en.ts
Write: /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/extension/i18n/pt.ts

File shape (exactly):
```ts
import type { ExtensionMessages } from "./en";

export const pt: ExtensionMessages = {
  ...same keys, same nesting, same function signatures (parameter names may stay, drop the `: string` type annotations since they're inferred)...
};
```
Rules:
- Translate every string value; keep keys, structure and `${...}` interpolations exactly. Keep "Heard", "Deepgram", "Chrome", "Chrome Web Store", "console.deepgram.com", URLs and "→" unchanged. `introBefore`/`introAfter` wrap a link to console.deepgram.com, so the sentence must read naturally around it.
- Match the terminology and voice already used on the website for this language: read /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/i18n/messages/pt/watch.ts and key.ts (how they say captions/legendas, transcript, API key, tab/aba). Use the same words. Plain, short, sentence case. Typographic quotes/apostrophes like the site.
- Labels like overlay.status are short.
- Don't edit any other file. Don't run git.
- When done, run: cd /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/extension && PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin:$PATH npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json 2>&1 | grep "i18n/pt" ; fix only errors in your file (others may be mid-edit by someone else; ignore them). Reply with one line saying done.
